A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciMDR work. The main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison; visual inspection confirms that the rasterized appendix examples in v1 correspond to those in v2.

before.justification: Tables 3–8 report original benchmark evaluations, fine-tuning comparisons, ablations, context-noise experiments, and failure analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a manual evaluation of 300 synthetic training examples in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The claim-centric synthesis, visual grounding, backward reasoning generation, document-scale regrounding, and staged fine-tuning procedures are unchanged. The synthesis prompts in Appendix C also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SciMDR training corpus, SciMDR-Eval, ChartQA, CharXiv, SPIQA, and context-noise scenarios. The new manual audit samples existing training data without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same comparator sets, including SPIQA fine-tuning, the open multimodal models, and GPT-4o/5.1/5.2. The newly cited SciRIFF work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces author review of 100 examples per QA modality using correctness and relevance criteria. Table 6 also changes the reported localization flag for the 16.9-score ablation from present to absent, indicating removal of both localization and reasoning. This does not establish that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct manual audit of synthetic-data correctness and grounding. The existing data-quality comparisons, ablations, noise tests, and 100-question failure analysis remain; Section 5.3.4 summarizes failure analysis already present in v1 Appendix A.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new manual audit reports sample counts and judgments without adding uncertainty or annotator-agreement estimates.

E6.justification: Appendix A.3 newly reports all 100 VQA and 100 TQA examples as correct and grounded, and 91/100 MQA examples as high-quality and fully accurate. The other nine MQA examples are described as factually correct but verbose or high-level. Numerical scores in Tables 3–8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The new limitations discuss informal assumptions about teacher-model reliability without introducing mathematical definitions, derivations, or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the synthesize-and-reground framework, SciMDR training dataset, SciMDR-Eval benchmark, and improved scientific QA through fine-tuning. The shortened title and wording edits do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v1 briefly mentions proprietary-model dependence and STEM focus. v2's new Limitations section explains how teacher errors and biases can propagate into training signals and explicitly states that applicability to Humanities and Social Sciences remains unvalidated.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, input limits, preprocessing, evaluation software, synthesis and judge prompts, annotation documentation, and code/data links remain unchanged. The new audit's sampling and judgment procedure is an evaluation-protocol addition.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wadden et al. (2025), SciRIFF, to the introduction and bibliography. The broader related-work discussion and positioning around scale, faithfulness, and realism remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, standardizes benchmark typography, nests the existing analyses under Section 5.3, and adds a main-text failure-analysis summary, acknowledgements, and limitations. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 5–7 are resized and rearranged, several captions are shortened, and appendix material shifts. Figures 9–13 retain the same examples and layouts but have sharper graphics and extractable text in v2.

improvement.justification: The new 300-example audit provides limited direct evidence for synthetic-data quality, while explicit teacher-error and domain limitations improve qualification of the claims. Clearer ablation labeling and sharper appendix figures also help. The audit remains author-conducted without reported agreement or uncertainty, so the overall gain is modest.
